title: Gratitude Everyday
subtitle: Specific, said out loud — and the verse people misuse.
objectives: Name the four kinds of gratitude
Explain the difference between thanks in and thanks for
Say gratitude specifically and out loud

cards.title: Gratitude that nobody hears changes nothing
cards.text: It is not a mood you work yourself into. It is noticing something specific and then saying it to the person who did it.

cards.title: Specific, or it does not count
cards.text: The difference between a mood and a fact is a detail.
points: **"Thanks for everything"** is forgettable.
**"Thanks for waiting for me"** is not.
**Name the thing.** Then name the person.
**Psalm 103:2** — the command is against *forgetting*.

cards.title: Six buttons
cards.text: Tap each kind. The last two are the ones that go wrong.

question.explain: A detail turns a mood into a fact.

cards.title: In all circumstances, not for all circumstances
cards.text: This is the verse most often used badly.
points: **1 Thessalonians 5:18:** give thanks *in* all circumstances.
**It does not say be thankful for everything** that happens.
**You are not asked to be glad a thing was bad.**
**You are asked to find what is still true** while it is.

question.explain: A real difference, and the whole weight of the verse.

cards.title: Ten were healed. One came back.
cards.text: The story is not about the healing.
points: **Ten men were healed** on the way.
**One returned to say so.**
**The other nine were not ungrateful** — they were glad.
**They just did not say it.** That is the whole gap.

cards.title: You notice a fan when it stops
cards.text: Everything that works is invisible, which is the actual problem with gratitude.
points: **A working fan is background noise.**
**A broken one is all you can think about.**
**Your attention is built to find faults**, not functions.
**So noticing what works is deliberate work.**

cards.title: A maintenance log is a record of what held
cards.text: Mechanics keep one, and reading it back is an accidental gratitude practice.
points: **Every part that was replaced** is in there.
**So is every part that never needed it.**
**You forget the second list** entirely.
**Write things down** and you stop forgetting them.

cards.title: Comparison is the off switch
cards.text: You cannot be grateful and be counting someone else's total at the same time.
points: **Someone is always stronger or faster.**
**That will be true at every level**, forever.
**Compare to your own last month** instead.
**That comparison has an answer** you can act on.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Name the specific thing, and say it out loud.
Thanks *in* all circumstances, not *for* all circumstances.
Luke 17 — nine were glad and said nothing.
Comparison turns gratitude off.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 2 Devotion. Gratitude is defined as an action with a detail in it rather than a mood, because a mood cannot be practised and a sentence can. The week does careful work on 1 Thessalonians 5:18, which is routinely used to tell people to be glad about bad things: the text says thanks *in* all circumstances, and the distinction is given its own card and two questions. Luke 17 is read precisely — the nine were glad and did not say so — which is a more useful reading than calling them ungrateful. The teardown lens gives the mechanism: attention is built to find faults, so noticing what works is deliberate.
discussion: Ask for one specific thank-you, named, out loud.
Ask the difference between thanks in and thanks for.
Ask what the nine in Luke 17 actually did wrong.
Ask what comparison does to gratitude.
extension: Have him say one specific thank-you to one person each day for a week.
Have him list five things that worked today and nobody noticed.
misconceptions: "The verse says be thankful for everything." In, not for.
"The nine were ungrateful." They were glad and silent.
"Gratitude is a feeling." It is a sentence somebody hears.
